- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly, especially after spikes.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or neutral (0.00), model often underestimates; adjust upward, particularly in early/medium horizon.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >75.0), model frequently overcorrects or overshoots in next 3–5 days; cap forecast at +5–10% below peak.
- Model shows strong mean reversion bias in 30-day horizon — if forecast is >75.0, reduce by 1–2 points; if <70.0, raise by 1–2 points.
- Sentiment reversal (e.g., from +0.67 to -0.33) triggers model lag — delay forecast adjustment by 1–2 days; don’t react to sentiment shift until 2nd day.
- If sentiment is flat (0.00) for 3+ consecutive days, model tends to drift toward historical mean — anchor forecast to 30-day rolling average if no strong sentiment signal.
- Overshoots after sentiment spikes are common — apply “sentiment decay” rule: reduce forecast by 0.5–1.0 point per day after sentiment drops below 0.67.
